pain.title: Host and Live Ops lack one shared view of repeated chat questions, product interest, and offer checks during a live session, slowing and fragmenting their response.

assumptions.title: Mock Hackathon catalog values: fictional 400 mL shampoo, THB 299 list price, THB 105 product cost, and a 12% platform fee on net sales after discount.
assumptions.validation_needed: Confirm the synthetic values are suitable for the demo; do not present them as real product data or actual platform pricing.

assumptions.title: Mock audience sample: 250 average concurrent viewers; 30 unique viewers ask about a shampoo promotion in two minutes across 47 related messages (12% viewer share).
assumptions.validation_needed: Confirm the synthetic sample supports a clear Hackathon demonstration; it is not real audience analytics.

assumptions.title: For the short Hackathon demo, start the simulated live countdown at 3 minutes; coupon expiry follows the end of that mock live.
assumptions.validation_needed: Confirm that a 3-minute countdown is the right short demo duration; this is a mock timer, not platform data.

constraints.title: Current discovery and product scope is limited to the Hackathon demo; post-event product planning, commercial customer validation, and revenue model are out of scope.
In the Hackathon demo, recommend a promotion only when (sales after discount − product cost − platform fees) ÷ sales after discount is at least 10%.
Send promotion recommendations to Live Ops first; when Live Ops approves, simulate issuing the promotion to viewers immediately. A rejected recommendation is not issued.

For the Hackathon demo, use a rolling two-minute ratio of unique viewers asking about the same product/promotion to average concurrent viewers; AI groups equivalent questions and shows the ratio/trend rather than triggering from raw message count.
The Host view should provide concise talking points for the Host to phrase in their own words, not a ready-to-say script.
Show the promotion recommendation as pending in the Host view while Live Ops reviews it; after approval-triggered simulated issuance, show it as approved.

After Live Ops approves, show the simulated issued promotion as a viewer-facing banner on the mock live video/chat, including product, discount, discounted price, and a mocked countdown to the end of the live; no real platform connection is required.

AI should recommend a demand-appropriate discount based on viewer-interest ratio and product economics, not automatically maximize it. If the proposed discount would breach the 10% margin floor, reduce the discount until it meets the floor, then send the offer to Live Ops for approval.
Use fictional shampoo and simulated catalog values in the Hackathon demo; do not present the fixture as real product or platform data.
For this synthetic shampoo case only, show the mock AI recommending 15% off at 12% viewer interest; calculated margin is 46.7%. This is not a fixed discount rule.
The Host view should show product name and size, selling points, usage, price, and stock from the mock catalog alongside audience-interest summaries and talking points.
When AI adjusts a discount to meet the 10% margin floor, show Live Ops the original and adjusted discounts, explain why it changed, and show the margin for both versions.

If Live Ops rejects a promotion, show the Host that it was not approved, include the reason if Live Ops provided one (reason is optional), do not issue the promotion, and end the flow without automatically generating an alternative.
Treat the approved mock promotion as a time-limited coupon that expires when the live session ends; show the Host a countdown when it is released.
When the approved mock coupon is released, reserve the simulated stock; if it expires at the end of the live session without a completed purchase, return the reserved stock.
Provide separate working views for the Host and Live Ops.
Show the Host the current audience interest count, product clicks, add-to-cart count, product price, and stock.
